Checked the XOR fix against research/claims.json. limit-linear explicitly supports 'cannot compute functions like XOR' for single-layer networks. perceptronMath.ts trains through 64 random A-units (N_A=64, FAN_IN=10), and a random association layer can make XOR separable. issuesMerged.problem: Depth stops at 'just how simple' (55.55-56.4 s). The film says what the machine could learn and never shows what it could not. During the Minsky and Papert sentence the only pictures are the two success plates (vertical and horizontal bar) and the stamp. A 15-year-old is left asking 'simple compared to what?', and an expert sees the film's one real limitation (linear separability, the XOR result in limit-linear) stated but never taught. This is now the main thing holding depth below 8.
issuesMerged.fix: On 'showed just how simple' (55.55 s), add a third small plate after the divider, captioned 'one bar or the other, not both' in the plate-label face. Run it on the real trainPerceptron illustration model: the lantern stays cold, the needle swings back and forth across the threshold for a few tries, and the plate is tagged 'beyond it'. IMPORTANT: use two DISJOINT bars, for example a left vertical bar and a right vertical bar that share no cell. A crossing pair (+) that shares a centre cell is linearly separable for this model (a large weight on the shared cell suffices), so it would not fail, and the picture would then be false. Only ship the failing animation if the actual training run fails to converge; never hand-animate failure. Keep the 'an illustration of the rule' framing, because the Mark I's random association layer makes the hardware story subtler than the single-layer picture (claims limit-linear, mk1-patchboard). Hold the three plates until the iris begins (about 58.2 s).

summary: Round 3 FAILS the gate, but it is close: mean 7.83 (round 2: 7.43). Every dimension rose. accuracy 8.42 and sync 8.17 clear 8. clarity 7.92, story 7.92, visual 7.83 and sound 7.83 sit just under it, and depth 7.17 and curiosity 7.42 trail. No critical issues. The highest-leverage fix is to SHOW the limit: a real, failing single-layer XOR mini machine on 'just how simple', with a visible dim on 'years' and an unresolved 'wrong' cell in m01. Then: fix the nudge-push text collision (confirmed at 38.0 s), give the ending clear air (ceiling 66 → 68 s, tail hold, m01 last chord re-fit), plant Rosenblatt in the lab instead of walking him in (third round), fix the bookend head tangent, and add a pause after 'Nobody gave it the rule'.
